record.context_brief: Polynomial diameter bound for Cayley graphs of symmetric groups.
record.original_question: For a generating set T of the symmetric group S_n, let Gamma(S_n, T) be the Cayley graph with vertex set S_n and edges [g, gt] for g in S_n and t in T. Does there exist an absolute constant c such that for every n and every generating set T of S_n, the diameter of Gamma(S_n, T) is less than n^c?

evidence.quote: Prove (or disprove) that there exists a constant c such that for every n and for every set T of generators of the symmetric group S_n, the diameter of Gamma(S_n, T) is less than n^c.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. For any generating set $T \subseteq S_n$ of $S_n$, define the Cayley graph $\Gamma(S_n, T)$ to be the graph with vertex set $S_n$ and an edge between $g$ and $gt$ for every $g \in S_n$ and every $t \in T$. The diameter $\mathrm{diam}(\Gamma(S_n, T))$ is the maximum, over all pairs of vertices, of the length of a shortest path between them.

Determine whether there exists an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that for every positive integer $n$ and every generating set $T$ of $S_n$,
$$\mathrm{diam}(\Gamma(S_n, T)) < n^c.$$
Either prove the existence of such a constant $c$, or exhibit a sequence of generating sets demonstrating that no such constant exists.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a special case of Babai's conjecture for symmetric/alternating groups and remains open. The best known general bound is the quasipolynomial bound $\exp(O((\log n)^4 \log\log n))$ due to Helfgott and Seress (Annals of Math., 2014); a polynomial bound $n^c$ has not been established. Subsequent work (e.g., on classical groups with random generators) has continued in related directions but has not closed this case.

status_evidence.title: On the diameter of permutation groups
status_evidence.snippet: Helfgott and Seress prove a quasipolynomial diameter bound exp(O((log n)^4 log log n)) for Sym(n) and Alt(n).
status_evidence.claim: The best known upper bound on the diameter of Cayley graphs of S_n is quasipolynomial, not polynomial, so the polynomial conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Babai's conjecture for high-rank classical groups with random generators
status_evidence.snippet: Babai's conjecture remains open in general; partial results address specific families and random generating sets.
status_evidence.claim: The polynomial diameter conjecture (Babai's conjecture) is still open for symmetric groups in full generality.
